claim_comment: Closing the Native memory seam audit after validating the machine-readable authority map against the real repository and its public operation catalogs.
retry_note: The first completion run found the issue-scoped applied slot occupied by the earlier claim. That claim is archived in .beads/operations/history/tdmem-0103.claim.json and the completion slot was rotated without changing Beads issue state.
acceptance_criteria: All production memory entry points are listed.
Current write owner and read authority are named for each path.
Generated/derived surfaces are separated from canonical stores.
Likely provider seams are ranked by invasiveness.
close_reason: Mapped the complete TraceDecay Native memory production surface, named every authority, separated canonical and derived state, and ranked the viable provider seams.
close_comment: Evidence: product/architecture/native-memory-surface-map.json enumerates all retained HTTP, MCP, CLI, and SDK memory operations plus dashboard, hook, automation, retrieval, privacy, maintenance, and graph-reconciliation entry points. The paired Markdown explains end-to-end call paths. scripts/product/check-native-memory-surface-map.py validates the map against real source markers, catalogs, generated SDK descriptors, and repository paths; tests/product_native_memory_surface_map_test.py covers missing operations, route drift, authority drift, derived-state drift, observation isolation, seam ordering, and stale source references. The clean V2 baseline receipt remains product/baseline/tracedecay-v2-pr707-linux.json.
